body: Modern agent systems assemble capabilities at runtime, and this dynamic composition has recently received a complete formal treat ment in the spatiotemporal-composability calculus, in which a capability is a component carrying a tracked inverse, and agents are assembled as plugins. This plugin form is carried by a single process sharing one context, a carrier that places all components in one physical failure domain, a fault suspends every component at once, and process death interrupts every session the process hosts. This paper shows that neither the modeling nor the calculus binds an agent to one process, the statelessness of the language model keeps all cross-step state outside the model, and the soundness invariant is defined on the state space alone. These observations condense into four lemmas whose premises are the hypotheses of the calculus and the statelessness of language-model inference. On these lemmas this paper constructs Logos, a ROS-like cross process agent harness in which a plugin is a process and the only shared state is an append-only transcript. Eighty sessions resume with no repeated effect after kills placed at the four boundaries of the tool-call cycle, and a same-fault comparison with a single process reference configuration shows one fault interrupting every co-resident session while under the peer-process construction one fault ends at one node.
summaryZh: 现代智能体系统通常在单个进程中动态组合各种能力，但这导致了所有组件处于同一物理故障域的隐患。本文通过将大语言模型的无状态推理与形式化演算结合，构建了Logos——一个类似ROS的跨进程智能体底座。在该架构中，插件以独立进程运行，唯一的共享状态是只读/追加日志（transcript），有效提升了系统容错性与故障隔离能力。

glossary.explanationZh: 用于管理、编排和执行大模型智能体工具调用及生命周期的底层运行环境。
跨进程通信总线，用于在不同进程或节点之间传输消息与共享状态。
指语言模型本身不保留跨步骤的内部状态，所有历史和上下文均由外部显式维护。
故障隔离机制，确保单个组件或进程崩溃时不会波及或中断系统中其他健康组件的运行。
